findings.summary: A briefed blind spot recorded as kind Proposal fails WorkItem::validate, so the steward run fails on the missing-token case.
findings.evidence: blind_spot_change builds `evidence: Vec::new()`. The plan's decide() sets `kind = WorkItemKind::Proposal` whenever a brief is present. WorkItem::validate returns Err("a work item that is not a blind spot cites its evidence") when kind != BlindSpot and evidence is empty. run() calls `item.validate().map_err(...)?` for every decided item, so the whole run returns Err. Nothing is committed. The cli test `a_missing_token_reaches_the_owner_with_its_brief...` would fail. So would the planned core assertion that `item.validate()` is Ok for a briefed blind spot. Fix: Choose one approach and test it. (a) Have blind_spot_needing_owner give the item evidence, for example `vec![Reference::path(source)]` or the source reference. (b) Keep the item's own kind (BlindSpot), and make open_proposals and find_open accept any undecided item that has a brief. In both cases, add a test that runs steward::run (or the cli end-to-end test) on a briefed github blind spot and asserts that the run succeeds and the commit holds the item.
findings.location: Decision 1 / Step 3-4 (decide sets kind Proposal for briefed items; blind_spot_needing_owner = blind_spot_change + brief); crates/athena-core/src/steward.rs:739-749, 1327-1329; crates/athena-data/src/records/work.rs:131

findings.summary: The owner decisions page still routes by rung, not by brief, so env/token briefs never reach the owner's decision page.
findings.evidence: needs_owner returns true only when the rung is above the role's limit or the role is unrecorded. A steward GH_TOKEN item is at Implementation, which is within defaults-conventions, so line 370 skips it. read_snapshot keeps only kind Proposal items. Unbriefed above-limit items still show there as "No brief written yet". This is the surface the rejected job's findings 1 and 2 were about. The plan admits the effect and defers it, and no test covers the entry. Fix: Bring xtask/src/decisions.rs in line with the same rule: an undecided item is for the owner exactly when it has a brief. Update its tests (the 'No brief written yet' card and the within/above/unknown cases near lines 500-530 and 600-630), and list the file as a needed change. If xtask must stay out of scope, the plan should say that the owner will not see env/token briefs on the decisions page, and the docs and CHANGELOG should not claim otherwise.
findings.location: Dependents: 'owner decisions page' entry; Open questions; xtask/src/decisions.rs:94-96, 286, 369-372

findings.summary: An unbriefed above-limit item is recorded and then never seen by anyone, and its key blocks the steward from raising it again.
findings.evidence: run() seeds `seen` from known_keys, which come from all recorded work items (steward.rs:1286, 1322-1325). Under the new rule such an item is in neither open_proposals nor the drain. So it is permanently silent, and the steward will not raise it again. Fix: Add this as a stated risk, and say in the docs where such items can still be seen (records only). Alternatively, leave their keys out of `seen`, so a later run can raise them again with a brief if they turn into an env/token need.

findings.summary: Approving a GH_TOKEN brief queues a code job, but what the owner actually has to do is supply a token.
findings.evidence: The plan says that approving a briefed blind spot 'queues the make-readable job'. The owner action the brief asks for is an environment change, which no producer job can make. Fix: Have the prompt and brief wording put the owner action in if_yes (for example, 'set GH_TOKEN, then approve'). Or note in the docs that approve-work is only used after the owner has supplied the token.
findings.location: Dependents: 'deciding a proposal by id' entry; work_decisions.rs approve_request

summary: The plan routes owner decisions by whether a change has a brief, and enforces that in code (decide, open_proposals, in_limit). That fits the accepted reading, and the plan correctly keeps the audience role's unbriefed in-limit items working. Two problems need fixing first. (1) Blocker: the main case breaks. A blind spot with a brief has no evidence, because blind_spot_change sets evidence to an empty Vec. The plan turns that item into kind Proposal. WorkItem::validate (records/work.rs:131) refuses a non-blind-spot item with no evidence, and steward::run (steward.rs:1328-1329) passes that error up with `?`. So a missing-GH_TOKEN report would make the whole steward run fail, and the plan's criterion-2 end-to-end test could not pass. (2) Major: the owner decisions page (xtask/src/decisions.rs) still routes by rung. It would hide the GH_TOKEN brief and keep showing unbriefed above-limit items as "No brief written yet". The plan knows this and defers it to an open question, but that page is the only place the five-field brief is shown to the owner. Athena already raised the two fixture-file scope findings; they are justified and not repeated here. Everything else checks out against the code: the line numbers, the budget arithmetic and seam, records.rs:2265, and the refusal corpus.
